findings.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe action dereferences current_user and the TopicUser record without nil guards, so the endpoint 500s for logged-out users and for users with no TopicUser row. A user who clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link from an email while not logged in gets NoMethodError on nil.id (current_user is nil); a logged-in user who never visited the topic (no TopicUser row, e.g. notified via @mention with auto-tracking not persisted yet) gets NoMethodError on nil.notification_level — both return 500 instead of a redirect to login or a graceful no-op.

[BUG] The template is placed at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, but the route is registered as a top-level this.route('topicUnsubscribe') whose default template lookup resolves to templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, so the rendered template is never found. Navigating to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe renders an empty page (no renderTemplate override exists in routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 to point at the nested path), making the whole client-side feature inert.

[ADVISORY] afterModel unconditionally sets a property on topic.details, but the show payload for anonymous or permission-denied responses can omit details. A 403/serialized response without details causes a NoMethodError (set on null) in the promise chain, breaking the route transition for users without topic access.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe state mutation happens on a GET request handled by an action that also skips check_xhr, so the same-URL redirect path (slugless route) re-triggers the mutation after the 301 redirect to the canonical slug URL. Every unsubscribed visit through the slugless email link applies the toggle twice (once on the bare-id request before redirect, once on the redirected request), so a user who muted, then re-enabled notifications elsewhere and re-clicks an old email link gets muted again — and any prefetching crawler (e.g. Gmail image proxy or link scanner) permanently mutes the user's topic without consent.

[BUG] The rewritten unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but only send_notification_email passes unsubscribe_url into the message builder, so every other email built with add_unsubscribe_link crashes when rendering its HTML part. Emails such as digests and any other notification mailers that set add_unsubscribe_link without an unsubscribe_url opt raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument inside Email::MessageBuilder#html_part (lib/email/message_builder.rb:64), silently killing message delivery for entire mailer categories — a regression on paths this diff never touched.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe calls tu.notification_level on a TopicUser found by find_by(user_id:..., topic_id:...), which is nil whenever the recipient has no existing TopicUser row for the topic. A user who receives the notification email (e.g., watching a category or via group mention) but has never visited that topic clicks the emailed unsubscribe link and gets a 500 from NoMethodError on nil:notification_level instead of a working unsubscribe page.

[BUG] TopicsController#unsubscribe dereferences current_user.id without any login guard, and the route is a plain GET with check_xhr skipped but no require_login. Any anonymous visitor (or logged-out recipient of a forwarded email) who opens the unsubscribe URL gets a NoMethodError on nil:id 500 response instead of a sign-in redirect or a friendly error.

[ADVISORY] The new unsubscribe action — including its two-way toggle semantics (tracking→regular, regular→muted), slug-redirect branch, and perform_show_response HTML path — is behavior-bearing new controller logic with no spec anywhere in this diff (the only test change is message_builder_spec.rb asserting List-Unsubscribe header presence). A future refactor of TopicUser.notification_levels or of perform_show_response silently breaks the emailed unsubscribe flow for all users, and no test in the suite fails; the toggle's asymmetric semantics in particular are completely unverified.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe route's model hook calls PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id), a method whose existence is assumed but never verified or tested in this diff, and the promise rejection path (topic not found, no access) is unhandled. If loadTopicView is absent or errors (deleted/private topic, stale email link), the Ember route rejects with no error template, leaving users who clicked the email link on a blank/error screen with no way to complete the unsubscribe the email promised.

[BUG] The unsubscribe GET endpoint crashes with NoMethodError when the email recipient is not logged in (current_user is nil). A user clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link from their email client without an active session; TopicView.new succeeds but `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, ...)` raises NoMethodError on nil.id, returning a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page — the feature's primary flow fails.

[BUG] `tu` is nil and the action raises NoMethodError on `tu.notification_level` when no TopicUser row exists for the (current_user, topic) pair. A logged-in user who receives a notification email (e.g. via @mention) but has never opened the topic has no TopicUser record; clicking the emailed unsubscribe link raises NoMethodError, 500s, and never unsubscribes them.

[BUG] The rewritten `unsubscribe_link` locale now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, which crashes every email built with add_unsubscribe_link: true whose mailer does not pass unsubscribe_url. Any MessageBuilder consumer other than send_notification_email that sets add_unsubscribe_link (the spec's other fixtures, and any system/test emails) hits I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (or emits a literal %{unsubscribe_url} link, depending on raise flag), breaking those emails — scope expansion from per-topic links into all unsubscribe-link emails.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe implementation duplicates notification-level mutation logic instead of using the existing TopicUser.change, which publishes MessageBus notifications. Users viewing the topic live are not told their notification level changed (no /topic/<id> MessageBus publish), and the 'muted if already regular' toggle behavior lives in a second place future changes must update; whoever changes TopicUser.change's semantics next gets silently divergent behavior from this path.

[ADVISORY] The property name is misspelled `stopNotificiationsText`, matched by the equally misspelled template reference. Works today only because template and controller agree on the typo, but any future rename/refactor searching for the correctly spelled name misses it, and the misspelling propagates into the component's public surface.

[ADVISORY] The diff mixes the per-topic-unsubscribe feature with large unrelated style-only rewrites (var→const/arrow conversion, hash-brace removal, whitespace churn) across topic_user.rb, topic-from-params.js.es6, message_builder.rb, and notification.html.erb. The reformatting inflates the diff, buries the behavioral change (the two-line topic_user `tracking` scope rewrite) in noise, and creates merge-conflict surface for anyone with in-flight changes to these files — none of this work is traceable to the unsubscribe requirement.

[ADVISORY] The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action has no test coverage anywhere in the diff. The nil-current_user and nil-TopicUser crashes above, the slug redirect, and the regular→muted toggle logic are all untested; a regression in the mutation would silently stop unsubscribing users (or mute them unexpectedly) with no failing spec.

[BUG] topics#unsubscribe calls current_user.id without any authentication guard on a route reachable by anonymous HTTP GET. Email clients and link-scanners (Gmail, Outlook safe-link prefetch) fetch every URL in an email unauthenticated before the user clicks; each hit raises NoMethodError on nil current_user, returning a 500 and leaving the unsubscribe flow dead for those users.

[BUG] unsubscribe calls tu.notification_level on a TopicUser row fetched with find_by, which returns nil for any user with no existing TopicUser record. A user who received a notification email but has no TopicUser row (row created only via visit/track paths; TopicUser.change is called after the email is already built) gets NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a working unsubscribe page.

[BUG] The unsubscribe state transition is a GET handler that toggles notification_level (tracking→regular, regular→muted) with no confirmation step and no guard against repeat requests. Any authenticated prefetch that follows the user's cookies (email client preview scanners, browser preload) silently mutates the user's notification state without consent, and a second click of the same stale email link flips the user from muted back toward a different state — a user 'unsubscribes' and is later resubscribed at regular by re-clicking the same link.

[ADVISORY] unsubscribe_link template now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}, but unsubscribe_url is only passed as an option in UserNotifications#send_notification_email, not added to Email::MessageBuilder's default template_args. Any other mailer that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without passing unsubscribe_url (e.g. digest or signup mailers) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when rendering, turning previously-working emails into delivery failures — the coupling is invisible at the template definition site.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe page is built as a second, parallel topic-loading path (store.createRecord + PostStream.loadTopicView + updateFromJson) duplicating the existing topic route/model pipeline. Topic serialization changes (fields added/renamed in TopicViewSerializer) must now be mirrored in two client pipelines; the unsubscribe path also never loads posts so details-dependent UI degrades silently, and any future fix to topic loading logic must be applied twice or the unsubscribe page drifts out of sync.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError for any user who has no TopicUser row or is not logged in. The email's unsubscribe link (post.topic.unsubscribe_url) carries no auth token; an anonymous or logged-out recipient clicking it hits current_user.id (nil) or TopicUser.find_by returning nil, producing a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page the email promises. Same crash for a logged-in user who never interacted with the topic (no TopicUser row).

[BUG] The GET unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification state with no confirmation and no CSRF-relevant flow, and only sets level to :regular, which does not actually stop notifications. Level :regular still delivers reply/mention/PM notifications per Discourse semantics, so the email copy "stop receiving notifications about this topic" is false for a watching/tracking user — the objective of the feature (per-topic unsubscribe) silently drifts to "downgrade one notch", and any link prefetcher (mail client scanners) triggers the mutation via GET without user intent.

[BUG] The frontend unsubscribe route loads the topic but never invokes the server-side unsubscribe logic, so the page shown contradicts the server state mutated only by the redirect-hit path. Visiting the canonical URL /t/slug/id/unsubscribe directly via the Ember route performs no unsubscribe and no redirect to the controller action, so users landing on the page are told "You will stop receiving notifications" while nothing changes — unless the slugless URL /t/id/unsubscribe was hit first to trigger the 301 redirect and the mutating GET.

[ADVISORY] The property name 'stopNotificiationsText' misspells 'Notifications' and is only accidentally functional because the template misspells it identically. The next developer who renames one side to the correct spelling breaks the unsubscribe copy silently (empty text on the unsubscribe page); a future template fix or Handlebars lint will surface this as a runtime blank.

[ADVISORY] The slug-mismatch redirect returns 301 (permanent) for a state-dependent unsubscribe URL, which lets browsers/mail clients cache a redirect that includes a one-time mutating destination. A cached 301 to /t/id/unsubscribe means revisiting or prefetching the email link re-fires the mutating GET on each request, re-toggling notification level (regular→muted→muted) — the user's state can flip without intent.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action performs a destructive state change (muting the topic) on an unauthenticated-token GET request with no CSRF protection or confirmation, so any cross-origin page or embedded image can trigger it (e.g. ``), silently muting the topic for the logged-in victim. An attacker embeds the unsubscribe URL of any topic in a third-party page; every victim whose browser loads it with a live Discourse session gets that topic muted without their knowledge — the user stops receiving notifications for the topic and is never told. The same is triggered by every email client prefetcher, link scanner, and Gmail/Outlook one-click-unsubscribe bot that follows the %{unsubscribe_url} in the email footer, muting the topic even though the user never clicked. Combined with the toggle logic (regular -> muted), a scanner that follows the link once permanently mutes the topic.

[BUG] `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` returns nil for any user who has never visited/tracked the topic, and the subsequent `tu.notification_level` call raises NoMethodError, returning a 500 instead of a graceful response. Any logged-in user who receives a notification email for a topic they have no TopicUser row for (e.g. via @mention on first contact) and clicks the per-topic unsubscribe link gets a 500 error and cannot unsubscribe; the email-scanner/prefetcher path from finding 1 also turns into a stream of 500s in production logs.

[ADVISORY] `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` triple-stash renders unescaped HTML built from the user-controlled topic title (`model.fancyTitle` interpolated into the I18n string containing `{{title}}`), so any markup present in fancyTitle is injected straight into the page. A user who can create or rename topics controls the title that lands in this unescaped sink; if fancy_title does not fully strip or escape angle-bracket markup (it preserves some HTML/entities by design), the unsubscribe page for that topic becomes an XSS vector for anyone who receives the notification email and clicks through. The safe pattern is to keep `` in the translation and use a normal `{{title}}` interpolation rather than making the whole string HTML.

[ADVISORY] The updated spec passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" to the builder but only asserts that header_args['List-Unsubscribe'] is present, never that the per-topic unsubscribe URL actually lands in the rendered message body via the %{unsubscribe_link} substitution in email/notification.html.erb. If the new unsubscribe_url template arg is dropped or malformed anywhere between message_builder.rb's template_args merge and the unsubscribe_link I18n interpolation (e.g. a key mismatch yields a raw %{unsubscribe_url} or an empty link), the spec still passes green because be_present on the header asserts nothing about the body content, so the shipped email contains a broken per-topic unsubscribe link that no test catches.

[ADVISORY] The spec's assertion `expect(...).to be_present` on the List-Unsubscribe header is a bare-existence assertion that passes regardless of whether the header contains the correct URL, so the newly supplied unsubscribe_url option is never verified against any output value. A regression that puts the wrong URL (e.g. the site base URL instead of the per-topic unsubscribe path) into the List-Unsubscribe header or the message body passes this suite unchanged, leaving email clients pointing users at the wrong destination.

[BUG] The unsubscribe action calls tu.notification_level on a nil TopicUser record, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 where the unsubscribe link promises a working page. Any user who received a notification email but has no TopicUser row for that topic (e.g., never visited the topic, row never created) clicks the emailed unsubscribe link and gets a raw 500 instead of the unsubscribe confirmation page; the level is never changed and no error state is shown.

[BUG] The unsubscribe route performs current_user.id without any authentication guard, so an anonymous visitor following the emailed link crashes the controller. A user who clicks the unsubscribe link from an email client without an active Discourse session (the common case — email links are opened logged-out) hits TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], nil) then current_user.id on nil, producing a 500 instead of a login redirect or 4xx.

[ADVISORY] The unsubscribe state mutation is performed via an unauthenticated-by-design GET request and bypasses TopicUser.change, so no MessageBus notification_level_change message is published. Users who complete unsubscribe on one device keep seeing the stale notification level on an already-open topic tab (no /topic/:id message pushes the change), and crawlers/prefetchers (e.g., email scanners prefetching GET links) can flip a user's notification level silently if a session cookie rides along; the mutation should go through TopicUser.change or be POST with a token.

[ADVISORY] The route's model hook has no rejection handler, so a failed PostStream.loadTopicView (e.g., the 301 redirect from slugs_do_not_match, or a 404 for a deleted topic) surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection with a blank error route instead of the app's standard error/not-found page. A user following an unsubscribe link for a deleted/removed topic or with a stale slug gets an Ember error dialog or blank page rather than the 'topic not found' experience other topic routes provide; debugging is misdirected because the route reports a generic transition error.

adjudication.rationale: The new route `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6` has `afterModel(topic) { topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null); }` with no guard for `details` being null/undefined. Doing this on a GET endpoint is a real correctness/security defect (can be triggered by link prefetchers/scanners or CSRF-style requests without explicit user intent). However, the specific claim that the slugless route toggles once and then toggles again after a 301 is not supported by the diff: the redirect guard (`return redirect_to ...`) happens *before* the `TopicUser` lookup/mutation, so the pre-redirect request does not apply the toggle.

If a caller sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not pass `unsubscribe_url`, this translation will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` at render time. The diff shows at least one caller updated to pass it (`send_notification_email` and the spec), but nothing in the diff guarantees all other `add_unsubscribe_link` usages now provide `unsubscribe_url`, so the new interpolation requirement can break existing email paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The unsubscribe state transition is a GET handler that toggles notification_level (tracking→regular, regular→muted) with no confirmation step and no guard against repeat requests. Any authenticated prefetch that follows the user's cookies (email client preview scanners, browser preload) silently mutates the user's notification state without consent, and a second click of the same stale email link flips the user from muted back toward a different state — a user 'unsubscribes' and is later resubscribed at regular by re-clicking the same link.

The controller action then **mutates state** by changing `TopicUser.notification_level` and saving (`tu.notification_level = ...; tu.save!`). Because this is a GET endpoint with side effects (and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]`), it is vulnerable to unintended triggering via link prefetch/preview while authenticated. However, the finding’s specific claim that a second click would flip a muted user back to regular is not supported by the code: once muted (`<= regular`), the `else` branch keeps it muted rather than toggling back.

The email's unsubscribe link (post.topic.unsubscribe_url) carries no auth token; an anonymous or logged-out recipient clicking it hits current_user.id (nil) or TopicUser.find_by returning nil, producing a 500 instead of the unsubscribe page the email promises. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The GET unsubscribe endpoint mutates notification state with no confirmation and no CSRF-relevant flow, and only sets level to :regular, which does not actually stop notifications. Level :regular still delivers reply/mention/PM notifications per Discourse semantics, so the email copy "stop receiving notifications about this topic" is false for a watching/tracking user — the objective of the feature (per-topic unsubscribe) silently drifts to "downgrade one notch", and any link prefetcher (mail client scanners) triggers the mutation via GET without user intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new GET route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) that directly mutates `TopicUser.notification_level` and `save!`s in `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, with no confirmation step and no non-GET/CSRF-relevant flow. This makes the endpoint vulnerable to unintended activation (e.g., link prefetchers/scanners) because merely requesting the URL performs the change. Also, for users with `notification_level > :regular` (e.g. tracking/watching), the code only downgrades to `:regular` (`tu.notification_level = ...[:regular]`), while the UI/email copy added claims “stop receiving notifications” (client text: `stop_notifications`, server email copy: “To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic…”), which is not guaranteed by a downgrade to `:regular` (it’s not an explicit “mute/stop all” action).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The frontend unsubscribe route loads the topic but never invokes the server-side unsubscribe logic, so the page shown contradicts the server state mutated only by the redirect-hit path. Visiting the canonical URL /t/slug/id/unsubscribe directly via the Ember route performs no unsubscribe and no redirect to the controller action, so users landing on the page are told "You will stop receiving notifications" while nothing changes — unless the slugless URL /t/id/unsubscribe was hit first to trigger the 301 redirect and the mutating GET.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds explicit Rails routes for `GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe` and `GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` mapping to `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which mutates `TopicUser` and then renders HTML via `perform_show_response`. So a direct visit to the canonical URL `/t/slug/id/unsubscribe` will hit the server-side unsubscribe logic (it is not “Ember-only”). While the Ember `topic-unsubscribe` route’s model hook (`PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`) does not itself call the unsubscribe endpoint, the finding’s central claim that visiting the canonical URL directly via the Ember route performs no unsubscribe/redirect is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The slug-mismatch redirect returns 301 (permanent) for a state-dependent unsubscribe URL, which lets browsers/mail clients cache a redirect that includes a one-time mutating destination. A cached 301 to /t/id/unsubscribe means revisiting or prefetching the email link re-fires the mutating GET on each request, re-toggling notification level (regular→muted→muted) — the user's state can flip without intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` triple-stash renders unescaped HTML built from the user-controlled topic title (`model.fancyTitle` interpolated into the I18n string containing `{{title}}`), so any markup present in fancyTitle is injected straight into the page. A user who can create or rename topics controls the title that lands in this unescaped sink; if fancy_title does not fully strip or escape angle-bracket markup (it preserves some HTML/entities by design), the unsubscribe page for that topic becomes an XSS vector for anyone who receives the notification email and clicks through. The safe pattern is to keep `` in the translation and use a normal `{{title}}` interpolation rather than making the whole string HTML.

Since `model.fancyTitle` derives from the topic title (user-controlled) and the diff shows no escaping/sanitization at this sink, any HTML present in `fancyTitle` would be injected into the page when rendered via triple-stash, creating an XSS risk.

Users who complete unsubscribe on one device keep seeing the stale notification level on an already-open topic tab (no /topic/:id message pushes the change), and crawlers/prefetchers (e.g., email scanners prefetching GET links) can flip a user's notification level silently if a session cookie rides along; the mutation should go through TopicUser.change or be POST with a token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The route's model hook has no rejection handler, so a failed PostStream.loadTopicView (e.g., the 301 redirect from slugs_do_not_match, or a 404 for a deleted topic) surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection with a blank error route instead of the app's standard error/not-found page. However, the finding’s specific claim about a 301 from `slugs_do_not_match` is not directly supported here because the Ember route loads via `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)` (not the Rails `topics#unsubscribe` endpoint), so the exact failure mode described can’t be fully confirmed from the diff.
